what: Protagonist Therapeutics develops peptide drugs and licenses them to larger companies. Its blood disorder drug rusfertide is partnered with Takeda, and an oral psoriasis candidate is partnered with Johnson & Johnson.
customers: Pharmaceutical partners who fund development and pay milestones and royalties.
money: milestone and development payments from Takeda and Johnson & Johnson
moat: A peptide chemistry platform that produces oral versions of drugs normally injected, which is what makes the partnerships worth large upfront payments.
risks: Revenue is lumpy milestone payments: it was $434M one year and $46M the next
No approved product of its own, so everything depends on partners' decisions
176 times the latest year's revenue, which makes the ratio meaningless
opportunities: $567M of cash against $10M of debt, which funds years of development
Analysts see about 47% upside, with 14 covering the stock
Rusfertide has completed late-stage trials in polycythemia vera and would pay royalties for years if approved
watch: Regulatory progress on rusfertide and the Johnson & Johnson psoriasis programme.
